# Draft:Ancient maritime archaeological sites near Livorno, Italy

The Roman shipwrecks of the Meloria Shoals (or the Livorno Port shipwrecks) refer to a series of ancient Roman maritime archaeological sites located near the Port of Livorno and the Meloria shoals in the Ligurian Sea. These wrecks, ranging from the Roman Republic to the late Imperial period, provide evidence of the maritime trade routes linking the Tuscan coast to Hispania, Gaul, and the Eastern Mediterranean.
Geographical context
The Meloria shoals are a series of rocky outcrops located approximately  northwest of the modern port of Livorno. In antiquity, the area served as a natural hazard for vessels navigating toward the Roman port of Liburna (Livorno) or the nearby naval hub of Portus Pisanus.
Significant wrecks
Archaeological surveys led by the Nucleo Operativo Subacqueo (Underwater Operational Unit) have identified several distinct sites:
Meloria A and B
Identified in the early 1990s, these sites consist of scattered cargo remains. **Meloria B** is notable for a high concentration of ribbed glass bowls (coppe costolate) and fine tableware dating to the early 2nd century AD. These finds suggest a cargo of luxury goods destined for the wealthy villas of the Tuscan interior.
The "Amphora" Wreck (Meloria C)
Located at a depth of approximately , this wreck contained a uniform cargo of Dressel 1 amphorae, typically used for transporting Italian wine. Based on the ceramic typology, the wreck is dated to the late Republican period (c. 1st century BC).
Porto di Livorno Amphora (2016 discovery)
In 2016, a well-preserved 2nd-century AD wine amphora was recovered directly from the seabed at the mouth of the Port of Livorno by the Guardia Costiera. The discovery confirmed that archaeological material remains embedded even within the heavily modified industrial zones of the modern harbor.
Trade and significance
The variety of cargo found—ranging from garum from Lusitania to obsidian blocks and fine glassware—demonstrates that the waters off Livorno were a major junction for the annona (state grain supply) and private commercial interests. The proximity to the Pisa shipwrecks site suggests that the Meloria wrecks represent vessels that failed to navigate the final approach to the riverine ports of the Arno.
